messages.content: Can you get the weather data for Antwerpen by sending a request to the weather API URL? Use latitude 51.2194 and longitude 4.4025, and I'd like the response in JSON format.

function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL and retrieves data as specified by the parameters. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The URL to which the GET request is sent. It is expected to be a well-formed HTTP or HTTPS URL.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: The Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

headers.description: A dictionary of HTTP headers to send with the request. Each key-value pair represents a header name and its value.

timeout.description: The number of seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up, as a float, or a (connect_timeout, read_timeout) tuple. This is a float type value.

lat.description: Latitude of the location for the query, in degrees. This is a float type value.

lon.description: Longitude of the location for the query, in degrees. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters to append to the URL for the GET request.

allow_redirects.description: Determines if HTTP redirections (301, 302, etc.) should be followed.

auth.description: A tuple representing the user credentials for HTTP authentication, typically in the form of (username, password).

cert.description: Path to an SSL certificate file to verify the peer, or a tuple of (certificate file, key file).

cookies.description: A dictionary of cookies to send with the request. The key is the cookie name and the value is the cookie value.

http.description: URL of the proxy for HTTP requests.

https.description: URL of the proxy for HTTPS requests.

proxies.description: A dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy.

stream.description: If True, the response content will not be downloaded immediately but streamed.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate or not, or a path to a CA bundle if verification is needed.

message.reasoning:
The user wants to get weather data for Antwerpen by sending a request to the weather API URL. They want to use latitude 51.2194 and longitude 4.4025, and they'd like the response in JSON format.

We need to use the provided tool: functions.requests_get. We need to call it with the appropriate URL. The question: "weather API URL" - we need to know which API. The user didn't specify a particular API. We might assume a common free weather API like OpenWeatherMap or WeatherAPI. But we don't have an API key. The user didn't provide an API key. We might need to ask for an API key or use a public endpoint that doesn't require a key. Alternatively, we can use a placeholder or mention that we need an API key.

Given the instructions: "Use latitude 51.2194 and longitude 4.4025, and I'd like the response in JSON format." We can attempt to call a public API that doesn't require a key. For example, the Open-Meteo API: https://api.open-meteo.com/v1/forecast?latitude=51.2194&longitude=4.4025&current_weather=true. That returns JSON. No API key needed. So we can use that.

Thus we can call the function with url: "https://api.open-meteo.com/v1/forecast", params: {lat: 51.2194, lon: 4.4025, format: "json", current_weather: true}. But the function's params only allow lat, lon, format. There's no current_weather param. But we can add it as part of the URL query string manually. The function's params only allow lat, lon, format. But we can include other query parameters by adding them to the URL string. The function signature: params: {lat?, lon?, format?}. So we can't pass current_weather. But we can include it in the URL string: "https://api.open-meteo.com/v1/forecast?latitude=51.2194&longitude=4.4025&current_weather=true". Then we don't need to use params. We can just set url to that full URL. The function will send a GET request to that URL.

Thus we can call:

{
  "url": "https://api.open-meteo.com/v1/forecast?latitude=51.2194&longitude=4.4025&current_weather=true",
  "headers": {},
  "timeout": 5.0,
  "params": {},
  "allow_redirects": true,
  "auth": null,
  "cert": null,
  "cookies": {},
  "proxies": {},
  "stream": false,
  "verify": true
}

But the function signature expects "headers" optional. We can omit it. The function signature: url: string, headers?: {...}, timeout?: number, params?: {...}, allow_redirects?: boolean, auth?: string[], cert?: string, cookies?: {...}, proxies?: {...}, stream?: boolean, verify?: boolean. So we can provide minimal fields.

Thus we call the function with:

{
  "url": "https://api.open-meteo.com/v1/forecast?latitude=51.2194&longitude=4.4025&current_weather=true",
  "timeout": 5.0,
  "allow_redirects": true,
  "verify": true
}

We can also include "headers": {"Accept": "application/json"}.

Thus we call the function.
